To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the absence of horizontal cell migration in Lim1-CKOs results in a reorganization of the outer retinal circuitry; 2) the initial targeting and stratification of rod and cone photoreceptors and bipolar cells in the OPL is normal, but the subsequent maintenance of the rod pathway is abnormal; 3) the retraction of rod photoreceptor terminals and the ectopic sprouting of rod and cone bipolar cell dendrites occur in a sequential and time-dependent fashion

the development of the rod and the cone pathways in the retina is independent of the presence of horizontal cells but requires the maintenance of horizontal cells for the correct assembly of the outer retinal circuitry.
horizontal cells are required for the maintenance of the OPL but are not required for its initial formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and plasticity of the outer retina, and the role of inhibitory horizontal cells in the formation of the outer pliciform layer.
the role of horizontal cells in the assembly and plasticity of the mammalian retina, and the implications of these findings for understanding retinal circuitry in health and disease.
the mechanisms of neuronal migration and the development and plasticity of retinal circuitry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
horizontal cells are not necessary for the development or assembly of rod and cone photoreceptor terminals and bipolar cell dendrites, but are necessary for their maintenance".
the horizontal cells do not have a role in the initial targeting of rod and cone photoreceptors, rod bipolar cell dendrite, and cone bipolar cell dendrite.
horizontal cells are essential for the normal development of the rod pathway, but not the cone pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the loss of horizontal cells during development leads to a retraction of the rod spherule layer and a sprouty growth of rod bipolar cells to reach ectopic rod spherule-like structures in the inner retina.
the loss of horizontal cells during embryogenesis does not affect the initial assembly of the OPL, but does affect the subsequent maintenance and refinement of the circuitry in the outer retina.
horizontal cells are required for maintaining the normal morphology of rod bipolar cells and cone pedicles, and for the normal distribution and stratification of cone bipolar cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
horizontal cells are required for the maintenance of the outer retina, not for its assembly.
the loss of horizontal cells during development leads to the collapse of the rod spherule layer, which in turn triggers rod bipolar dendrites to sprout and extend to ectopic ribbon-proteins.

the absence of horizontal cell processes in the OPL does not disrupt the assembly of the rod and bipolar pathways during development but rather causes a reorganization of the OPL that is not complete until well after birth.
